lecture_title: Boltzmann Weights, Partition Functions, and the Ideal Gas

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_02.png
assets.rationale: The augmented functional is complete across the board, no lecturer obscures it, and the terms constant under probability variation have already been removed.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Here's what we have to minimize.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_03.png
assets.rationale: Normalization, the mean-energy constraint, the partition function, and its beta derivative are simultaneously legible with only a small lower-right obstruction.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: I took the definition of z and differentiated it.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_04.png
assets.rationale: The full entropy differential and the simplified result dS equals beta dE are unobstructed, with the cancelled terms grouped on the board.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_05.png
assets.rationale: The momentum integral, dimensionless Gaussian variable, and square-root Jacobian are visible together while the lecturer stands clear of the central equations.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The integral is just a number.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_06.png
assets.rationale: The ideal-gas partition function is complete, sharp, and unobstructed; the lecturer is below and to the left of the formula.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Let me just show you what this n factorial does.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_07.png
assets.rationale: The final energy per particle and derivative of log Z are both complete and readable, while the lecturer does not cover either boxed result.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The energy per particle is three halves the temperature.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_08.png
assets.rationale: The infinite-atmosphere partition factors and both beta-dependent logarithmic terms are fully visible with no lecturer obstruction.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: another term which looks like n over beta
assets.caption_hint: gravitational partition function and energy terms
